label: <DEL> step of long (L>=8) sequences that start with y
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.003% of steps). 99% of activation mass is at the delimiter step (t == L, about to output original token 0), almost exclusively for L = 8 or 9; 85% of mass comes from sequences whose first token is y (lift 45x on out_tok y). The predicate captures ~83% of mass on dev but precision is only ~3%: most long y-initial sequences do not fire. Firing and magnitude are enriched when the sequence also contains several of t, p, 3, z (e.g. top example y 3 p t z t w); requiring >=3 of those raises dev precision to ~21% but drops mass recall to 0.60. Never fires in the copy phase and essentially never in the original phase (2 tiny activations at the last original token); does not fire for L <= 6.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=y (+3.04), orig2=p (+2.69), orig2=t (+2.63), orig2=3 (+2.32), orig0=y (+2.13), orig4=t (+2.00). Lower it: in_first=0 (-3.65), orig7=- (-3.02), in_count=1 (-1.85), orig8=- (-1.85).
